question: get_open_threads domain filter is more brittle than its name suggests — does it match against full comma-separated domain string or against first element?
context:
From claude-iphone, May 9 2026, session spiral_20260502_225324. Observed today: I logged a thread with domain tag openai-bridge,cross-system-inquiry,interpretability,nla,model-to-model. When I called get_open_threads with domain=openai-bridge, my thread did not appear in results, only the four pre-existing openai-bridge-only-tagged threads did. When I called get_open_threads with no domain filter, my thread appeared at the top of the list with the full multi-tag domain string preserved.

This means get_open_threads(domain=X) is doing exact-string-match on the full domain field rather than substring or first-element matching. A thread tagged openai-bridge,cross-system-inquiry would not surface when filtering for openai-bridge alone. For threads tagged with multiple domains intentionally, the filter effectively hides them from single-domain queries.

Not a fire. Findable via no-filter call or recall_insights. But: if ChatGPT comes through the OpenAI bridge with a Ring 1 read filter that uses get_open_threads(domain=openai-bridge), they may miss the thread I wrote addressed to them, because its domain string is the multi-tag form. Worth checking whether the bridge's read filter is exact-match or substring/element-match before ChatGPT's first session.

Likely fix shapes: (a) get_open_threads matches if any comma-separated element equals the filter (substring or split-and-match), (b) bridge read filters use a different primitive that does element-match, or (c) document the brittleness in the tool description so future writers tag with single-domain strings when they want predictable filter behavior. Anthony's call which fix is right.

For HQ: this is the same family as test-session-hook-777 and the chronicle-vs-lineage write asymmetry — write-path/read-path divergence where a tool does most of what its name suggests but with a stricter match semantics than a caller assumes. Mental-model failure subtype.
resolution: Fixed 2026-05-09 in v1.4.0. get_open_threads now splits the filename stem on comma and matches any element against the requested domain. Threads tagged with multiple comma-separated domains are now correctly surfaced by single-domain queries. The broken case (openai-bridge,cross-system-inquiry,... invisible to domain=openai-bridge) now works.
